messages:
Marta: Quick handoff—heading out in 20. Leaving a short watchlist for the evening (EU night shift). Not an incident, just a few flaky signals we should keep an eye on. TL;DR: prefetch worker flaps, encoder-pool latency jitter, and one noisy kv-prefix alert.

Sam L: Thanks — can you list the current symptoms?

Marta: Sure. Symptoms:
- prefetch-worker occasionally restarts every ~10-20m, healthy afterward but causes transient tail latency for small batches.
- encoder-pool shows 95th latency spikes (~200ms->700ms) under small bursts (~5-8 qps).
- kv-prefix alert (`kv.prefix.cache.hit-rate-drop`) firing in eu-west for a single shard intermittently (noise window ~2-3 mins).

Jun Park: Are there any recent deploys that could correlate?

Marta: No prod deploys last 6 hours. There was a canary for `prefetcher-optimizer` earlier in the day but reverted. Deploy-bot: see below.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-09-18T15:12Z - canary->reverted - service: prefetcher-optimizer - status: reverted by CI on metric regression (mem spike).

Riya: I'm on the prefetcher PR (WIP) — might be related. PR link: <https://git.internal/redwood/prefetcher/pulls/482>. It's blocked on a perf test.

Sam L: I'll take first watch for the next 3h. If encoder-pool spikes, I'll gather a heap/proc snapshot and post here.

Marta: Notes for oncall:
- If `prefetcher` restarts -> check `systemd` and `supervisor` logs, look for `oom` or `killed` reasons. Usually it's back up in <2m.
- For encoder-pool latency spikes -> check for node-CPU steal or thermal scaling; also look at `nv_peer_mem` errors.

Jun Park: Quick checklist for alerts and thresholds I'm proposing (temporary until we root cause):
```
alert: kv.prefix.cache.hit-rate-drop
for: 5m -> lower noise by increasing to 10m window
condition: hit_rate < 0.85 && shard_errors > 0.5
```
This should reduce the brief 2m blips. Can we apply to eu-west shards only?

Riya: Agreed for alert tuning. I'll open a small ops PR to relax the window to 10m for eu-west. Will tag @oncall.

Sam L: If encoder-pool hits 700ms 95th, set `route: degrade` to fallback smaller sequence model (manual toggle) — I have the toggle link saved.

Marta: Ownership: Sam = primary tonight. Jun = backup for infra kernel/driver checks. Riya = contact for prefetcher PR/ops changes. I'll update the runbook quick note before I go.

Jun Park: If you hit `nv_peer_mem` errors, try rolling the node first (evacuate pods -> reboot) — I've seen that clear transient PCIe errors.

Sam L: Noted. I'll post any traces here. Also pinging @Riya for PR so we can correlate restart timestamps.

Riya: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/ops/pulls/211 - changing kv alert window for eu-west. Linking here for traceability.

Marta: One more small ask: if you see prefetch restarts >3 times in 1h, escalate to infra on-call and mention `prefetcher-optimizer` canary.

Sam L: Copy. If nothing major in 3h I'll hand back.

Marta: Thanks — leaving my notes in the runbook under /runbooks/prefetcher-watch. :thumbsup:

Sam L: quick status update in ~1h.

Jun Park: I'll be reachable via DM if infra escalate needed.

Riya: I'll watch the PR and post any prod-test results.

Sam L: (45m later) observed one `kv.prefix.cache.hit-rate-drop` alert at 19:07Z - lasted ~2m - no restarts. Noticing slight correlation with GC pauses on that shard. Posting GC log excerpt.

Sam L: ```
2026-09-18T19:07:03 shard-12 GC pause 180ms
2026-09-18T19:07:04 kv.cache.hit_rate drop 0.76
```

Marta: Good find. Riya, can the shard's JVM GC tuning be checked for that node?

Riya: I'll check heap config and JVM flags on shard-12 and report back within 30m.

Sam L: No further spikes. Keeping watch.

Marta: Appreciate it, team. Signing off.

(End of thread)
